info.title: GovAuctions Data API
info.description: Structured government-surplus auction data. Live listings (facts only, no images) cover sanctioned federal sources (GSA Auctions) in the US. Sold-price comps and the proprietary GovAuctions Flip Score resale signal are derived aggregates; comps cover the full surplus market in US, UK, CA, AU, DE, FR (/sources lists each market's archive size). Every plan carries two budgets: total calls, and a smaller valuation allowance that the valuation endpoints (/comps, /comps/batch per query, /sold, /comps/trend, /flip-score) draw down — see the X-Valuation-* response headers, or call /usage to read both budgets directly. Past the monthly valuation allowance, a key that holds prepaid credits spends one per valuation call; a call that returns no answer (empty, not priceable, or an error) costs nothing from either. Listing prices and bid counts are refreshed on a twice-daily ingest (about 06:00 and 18:00 UTC); the listing endpoints serve that snapshot rather than polling the source per request, so a lot's bid can be up to ~12h behind. Check /coverage before building on the comp endpoints: it reports what we can and cannot price. Plans: Free (free); Pay as you go (prepaid credits from $10 for 500 valuation calls); Enterprise (contact us). Get a key at https://govauctions.app/developers.

get.summary: Search live listings (facts only, GSA Auctions)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Source platform (sanctioned sources only; currently gsa)

parameters.name: zip
parameters.description: US 5-digit ZIP to search around. Limits results to lots within radiusMiles, orders them nearest-first, and adds distanceMiles to each item plus an origin block to the response.

parameters.name: radiusMiles
parameters.description: Radius from zip, in miles. Requires zip.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Result order. Default is soonest-ending, or nearest-first when zip is given. `newest` orders by the lot's own listing date (auction start), newest first, with a deterministic id tie-break - use it for recurring "what's new" polling, where the default order can leave a brand-new lot off page one. Lots that have not opened yet sort to the top.

200.description: A page of listings. A zero-result page also carries a `scope` block naming the sources and market actually searched, so an empty `data` is distinguishable from "no such lots exist": raw listings are served for sanctioned public-domain sources only (gsa) in the US, while sold-price comps span the full market and all four comp markets (US, UK, Canada, Australia; the DE and FR markets carry live listings only and have no sold-price history).

get.summary: Get one live listing by id

200.description: Listing. Live lots only — this does not fall back to the sold archive.

get.summary: Sold-price range for a described item (full-market aggregate)

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Optional 2-letter state/region code for a regional range. Falls back to national when that state is too thin; the response `scope` field reports which pool was used.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Set to `comps` to also return the individual sales the range was computed from (title, finalBid, year, state, soldMonth). Sample size is capped by plan. Not served for EU markets (DE, FR, NL, PL): the range comes back with `compsWithheld: true`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many underlying sales to return with include=comps. Capped by the plan's sample limit.

200.description: Comp range (p25/median/p75), with scope=state|national when a state was requested, and `comps` when include=comps. A miss carries `data: null` plus a `reason`: `insufficient_comps` (too few comparable sales yet — worth retrying as the archive grows) or `category_not_priceable` (the requested category can NEVER return a range — the body lists them in `excludedCategories`). A catch-all category such as `miscellaneous` is NOT refused: the label is dropped and the item is priced on its title alone, and the body then carries `requestedCategory` + `categoryDropped` next to the `category` we actually resolved, so check `category` and `confidence` before trusting that range.

post.summary: Value up to N items in one request (one valuation call per query)
post.description: Send item descriptions and get one comp range per query. Each query costs one valuation call, the same as sending them separately. If the valuation allowance runs out mid-batch, the priced queries are returned and a `truncated` block names the rest.

queries.description: Item descriptions, or per-item objects {q, category, country, state}.

200.description: One result per query, in submission order

400.description: Malformed body, or more queries than the plan allows

get.summary: Month-by-month median sale price for an item
get.description: Sold-price trend built from the same matched comps as /comps, so the two can never disagree. Months with too few sales are dropped; a query without enough qualifying months returns an empty `data` array with a reason rather than a misleading two-point line.

200.description: Monthly medians plus a first-to-last change percentage

get.summary: The individual archived sales behind an item
get.description: Title, final price, sale month and state for the comparable sales behind a range, plus the range. Query-anchored: describe an item. No paging, id lookup, source platform, lot id or URL; this is evidence, not a browsable archive. Not served for DE, FR, NL or PL. Page size is capped by plan.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Capped by the plan's sample limit.

200.description: Matching sales, with a summary range

get.summary: How much comp data we hold, per category
get.description: Sales held per category for a market, each category's share of the pool, and the categories that can never return a range (real estate and junk-drawer buckets). Check this before building on the comp endpoints. Does not draw down the valuation allowance.

get.summary: Listing sources and comp markets this API covers
get.description: Live lot count per listing source, and archive size per sold-price comp market. Counts only. No key needed, and it does not count against any budget.

get.summary: This key's usage and remaining budgets for the month
get.description: Both counters and the reset date. The valuation allowance is the one that binds for comps-heavy traffic, and it is smaller than the headline call budget — read it here rather than inferring it from response headers. Does not draw down the valuation allowance.

200.description: Plan, period, call budget and valuation budget

post.summary: Create a webhook subscription (push on new lots)
post.description: We POST matching new lots to your https endpoint as they enter the feed. Payloads are raw per-lot records, so GSA only, like /listings. Signed with HMAC-SHA256 in X-GovAuctions-Signature; the secret is returned once, at creation. Delivery is at-least-once: dedupe on lot id.

201.description: Created; the response carries the signing secret once

403.description: Webhooks not in plan, or subscription limit reached

get.summary: GovAuctions Flip Score resale signal for one live lot, in any comp market
get.description: Any live lot from any source, in any market with sold-price comps (see the `country` enum on /comps). Returns our valuation and the link to the lot on its source site; no description or images. One lot per call; there is no way to list ids here.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Lot id, as it appears in a govauctions.app lot URL

200.description: Flip Score, estimated value, discount, country and sourceUrl

404.description: No live lot with that id in a comp market

get.summary: Bulk CSV export (pay as you go and above: buying any credit pack adds it). Row cap varies by plan.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Comps cover every market in this enum. Listings exports are US-only.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: For dataset=comps: comma-separated item descriptions, one row each (max 100); each charges one valuation call. For dataset=listings: a title keyword.

403.description: CSV export not included in plan

Listing.description: A live lot. Price fields describe BID state, which is not the same as the figure a source's own web page shows: GSA renders a lot's opening/minimum amount in a box labelled "Current Bid" even when nobody has bid, so treat currentBid, not the source page, as the answer to "has anyone bid".

currentBid.description: Highest bid actually submitted, or null when no bid has been placed. Null is a fact, not a gap: it means nobody has bid.

startingBid.description: Opening/minimum amount. ALWAYS null for gsa lots: the GSA Auctions v2 feed we ingest publishes no opening-bid field (its only price-related fields are highBidAmount, biddersCount, aucIncrement and reserve), so the opening figure shown on gsaauctions.gov is not available to us. Do not read null here as "no opening price".

bidCount.description: Bidders/bids reported by the source. Read together with bidStateUnknown: a 0 with bidStateUnknown absent means no bids, a 0 with bidStateUnknown true means the source did not report.

bidStateUnknown.description: Present and true only when the source publishes no bid state, making bidCount: 0 meaningless. Absent on gsa lots, which do publish bid state.

facts.description: Parsed attributes (year, make, model, ...) when derivable from the listing text.

bearerAuth.description: Your API key as a Bearer token (or send it as the x-api-key header).

x-versioning.scheme: URL path (/api/v1). A breaking change ships as /api/v2; /api/v1 is never broken in place.
x-versioning.additiveChanges: New endpoints, new optional parameters and new response fields can appear in v1 at any time. Ignore fields you do not recognise.
x-versioning.deprecationPolicy: A deprecated endpoint returns the RFC 8594 `Deprecation` header with the date it was deprecated and `Sunset` with the date it stops responding. Sunset is at least 180 days after Deprecation, and both are announced on /developers before they are sent.
